attributes.title: Level 2

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓Did you fill in all of the missing tiles on the tilemap with the three different tile options?
steps.senseiHelp:
Sample tilemap design:


Ask the ninja:

❓How might you edit the tilemap to make the project more of your own? What tiles would you change? 

❓Are there any other tiles you would add to improve the tilemap design?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Encourage the ninja to use both the paint and fill tools in the tilemap editor to complete the tilemap.

💡 Help the Ninja find the correct tiles, as needed. The green grass and dark purple tiles can both be found in My Tiles. The light purple brick tile can be found in the Gallery > Dungeon section.
steps.instructions:
Finish the tilemap design!


Edit the tilemap by clicking the square on the [set tilemap to] block. Click on My Tiles inside the tilemap editor. Then, fill in the missing tiles using the green grass tiles for the space inside the walls, and a mix of the light purple brick tile (from the Gallery) and the dark purple tile outside the walls.


Click ▶ to see your tilemap design.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type the correct coordinates into the [place sprite on top of] block so that the Player sprite starts on a light purple brick tile?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓How can you find a tile’s coordinates using the tilemap editor?

❓Why might you want the Player sprite to start on a light purple tile?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 A tile’s coordinates can be found by hovering your mouse over a particular tile and looking in the lower left corner of the tilemap editor.
steps.instructions:
Set the Player sprite’s position on the tilemap! 


Drag a [place sprite on top of] block into the [on start] container underneath the Player sprite’s [set sprite to] block. Select the Player sprite’s name and set the Player sprite’s starting position coordinates on a light purple brick tile . Find the coordinates by clicking the tilemap editor and looking on the bottom left corner as the cursor hovers over the tile. 


Notice that the Player sprite is able to move off the viewable screen. Drag in a [camera follow sprite] block under the [move sprite with buttons] block, then set it to the Player sprite.


Click ▶ to explore the tilemap by moving the Player sprite around the screen.

steps.hints: ❓Did you select the correct sprite name and the dark purple path tile in the [place sprite on top of random tile] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Why would you want the Key sprite to be placed on a random dark purple tile?

❓ What might happen when the Player sprite finds the Key sprite?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Explain to the ninja that randomness adds an element of surprise to the project. Ask the ninja to consider whether the game would be as fun to play if the Key sprite appeared on the same tile each time.
steps.instructions:
Set the Key sprite’s position on the tilemap!


Drag a [place sprite on top of random tile] block underneath the Key sprite’s [set sprite to] block. Select the Key sprite’s name, then select the dark purple path tile. 


Click ▶ and move the Player sprite around the tilemap to find the Key sprite!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type the column and row coordinates you found in the tilemap editor into the Castle sprite’s [place sprite on top of] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓How can you find a tile’s coordinates using the tilemap editor?

❓What should happen next, so that the Player sprite can reach the Castle sprite?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Encourage the ninja to think about the best placement of the castle on the green grass tiles. They may want the castle to be closer to the doors, so that the Player goes directly to it, or further inside, so that the Player still needs to move further in order to reach the castle.
steps.instructions:
Set the Castle sprite’s position inside the walls on the tilemap! 


Drag a [place sprite on top of] block into the [on start] container underneath the Castle sprite’s [set sprite to] block. Select the Castle sprite’s name and set the Castle sprite’s starting position coordinates on a green grass tile . Find the coordinates by clicking the tilemap editor and looking in the bottom left corner as the cursor hovers over the tile. 


Click ▶ to see that the Castle sprite is in a new position and the Player sprite cannot get to it through the walls.

steps.hints: ❓Did you type a message that appears when the Player sprite hits a tilemap wall?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ What happens when the Player sprite hits a tilemap wall? Which tiles are walls on the tilemap?

❓ What type of message will tell the Player where to go, before entering the garden?

❓Did you test out different parameters in the [camera shake] block?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Prompt the ninja to consider how the [on sprite hits wall] container block works. Whenever a sprite bumps into a tilemap wall (of any kind of tile image), the code inside the container will run.

💡Encourage the ninja to personalize the message in the [say] block. Although it should be directive for the Player, they can add their own spin to the language used.
steps.instructions:
Code a message that helps the Player sprite figure out how to get inside the garden wall!


Click Scene and drag out an [on sprite hits wall] container block. This event will make something happen whenever the Player sprite bumps into any wall on the tilemap. Drag a [camera shake] block into the container and adjust the 2 parameters to control how much the screen will shake.


Drag in a [say] block, use a (sprite) bubble from the container as the sprite name, and type a message telling the player to find the key in the string parameter, then adjust the time parameter to be 500ms. 


Click ▶ to see what happens when the Player hits a tilemap wall!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type 2 sets of column and row coordinates you found in the tilemap editor into the 2 [set wall at] blocks?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ How can you find a tile’s coordinates using the tilemap editor?

❓ Which tiles should no longer act as walls, after the Player overlaps with the Key sprite?

❓ Why does the [set sprite follow] block make it look like the Player is “holding” the Key?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Remind the ninja that they can find a tile’s coordinates by clicking the tilemap editor and looking on the bottom left corner as the mouse hovers over the tiles.
steps.instructions:
Code the Player sprite to pick up the Key sprite and unlock the doors! 


Drag a [set sprite follow] block into the [on (Player) overlaps (Key)] container. Set the Key sprite to follow the Player sprite using the container’s (otherSprite) and (sprite) bubbles.


Open Scene, then code the doors to “open” by dragging in 2 [set wall at] blocks underneath [set sprite follow]. Make sure the toggle is set to <OFF> then type in the coordinates of the 2 door tiles . Now, the doors will be unlocked as soon as the Player sprite collects the key; this will enable the sprite to pass through the tilemap walls to reach the Castle sprite.


Click ▶ then move the Player to “pick up” the key and unlock the garden wall doors!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you replace the tile image when the Player sprite overlaps the door tile so it looks like the wall doors “open”?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you select the wall tile in the [on sprite overlaps tile] container?

❓ Did you drag the (location) bubble into the [set tile at location] block?

❓ Did you add a message to the [say] block to welcome the Player sprite to the castle?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Encourage the ninja to personalize the message in the [say] block and the sound selected in the [play sound] block. Prompt the ninja to think about what else could happen when the Player sprite reaches the castle.
steps.instructions:
Unlock the doors with the key and make the garden wall doors “open”! 


Open Scene and drag out an [on sprite overlaps tile] container. Click the gray tilemap square and select the door tile. Drag in a [destroy sprite] block, and select the Key sprite to make it disappear when the doors open.  


Open Scene again and drag a [set tile at location] block. Select the green grass tile, then drag the (location) bubble from the container into the tilemap coordinate parameter. This will change the visual display of the tiles at either location that the Player sprite overlaps the door in. 


Use a [say] block to welcome the Player sprite to the castle, and a [play sound] block to add to the excitement of unlocking and opening the doors!


Click ▶ to see the doors “open” after the Player sprite collects the Key sprite, and how the key disappears when the Player sprite overlaps the door tiles.

steps.hints: ❓  Did you add fun customizations such as dialog text, animations, sounds, etc?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ What directions will help people understand how your project works?

❓How else might you update the tilemap design or add new sound, animation, or dialog effects to make the game more exciting?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Guide ninjas to note that while these customizing blocks are open ended and not required for the game to “work”, they really improve the Player’s experience playing a game, either by giving context to what the Player should do or not do, or to provide a more fun experience overall. They also allow the Ninja to add their personal touch and express themselves through small details present in the game.
steps.instructions:
Code the end of the adventure! 


Drag a [game over] block into the [on (Player) overlaps (Castle)] container. Set the toggle to <WIN> and add a [use effect] block above the [game over] block to choose a fun win effect.


Be sure to add directions at the beginning and experiment with animating sprites and/or adding music or screen effects.


Click ▶ to interact with the completed project and see the game over effects!

subgroups.introduction: Create a project that uses a tilemap and makes something happen when a sprite overlaps different tiles!

validationItems.text: Set the position of the Player sprite on a light purple brick tile, using tilemap coordinates. Set the camera to follow the Player sprite as it moves on screen with the direction buttons.
Set the Key sprite to appear on a random dark purple path tile.
Set the position of the Castle sprite inside the garden's walls, using tilemap coordinates.
Code the camera to shake and a message to appear when the Player sprite hits a tilemap wall.
On overlap, code the Player sprite to pick up the Key sprite, then turn the door tile “walls” OFF.

requirements.match:
sprites.onOverlap(SpriteKind.Player, SpriteKind.Key, function (sprite, otherSprite) {
    key.follow(wizard)
    tiles.setWallAt(tiles.getTileLocation(4, 3), false)
    tiles.setWallAt(tiles.getTileLocation(4, 4), false)

sprites.onOverlap(SpriteKind.Player, SpriteKind.Key, function (sprite, otherSprite) {
    otherSprite.follow(sprite)
    tiles.setWallAt(tiles.getTileLocation(4, 3), false)
    tiles.setWallAt(tiles.getTileLocation(4, 4), false)

sprites.onOverlap(SpriteKind.Player, SpriteKind.Key, function (sprite, otherSprite) {
    key.follow(wizard)
    tiles.setWallAt(tiles.getTileLocation(4, 4), false)
    tiles.setWallAt(tiles.getTileLocation(4, 3), false)

sprites.onOverlap(SpriteKind.Player, SpriteKind.Key, function (sprite, otherSprite) {
    otherSprite.follow(sprite)
    tiles.setWallAt(tiles.getTileLocation(4, 4), false)
    tiles.setWallAt(tiles.getTileLocation(4, 3), false)

validationItems.text: When the Player sprite overlaps a door tile, change each tile’s image and destroy the Key sprite.
End the game with a fun effect when the Player sprite overlaps the Castle sprite.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 2 of Orange Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about how to add events into your tilemap project. Events occur when a certain action triggers a set of code to run. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 2:

badges.title: Party Planner
badges.description: Use events to control actions in a project with a tilemap.

badges.title: Trip Wire
badges.description: Make something happen when a sprite overlaps a specific tilemap tile.

badges.title: Watch Out for That...!
badges.description: Make something happen when a sprite hits a tilemap wall.

badges.title: New Tile Who Dis?
badges.description: Use an event to change a tile on a tilemap.

badges.title: Birthday Party
badges.description: Use an event to make something happen when a sprite is created.

badges.title: Farewell Party
badges.description: Use an event to make something happen when a sprite is destroyed.

badges.title: Ticking Clock
badges.description: Set a sprite’s lifespan in a project.
